paper_title: Computing Generalized Rank Invariant for 2-Parameter Persistence Modules via Zigzag Persistence and Its Applications
statement: The algorithm Interval produces all intervals of an input interval decomposable module. What happens if the input module is not interval decomposable? We can show that the algorithm still produces intervals each supporting a submodule of an indecomposable of the input module (Figure 4), see [18] for details. Some other open questions that follow are: (i) Can we generalize Theorem 24 to d-parameter persistent homology for d > 2? (ii) Can the complexity of the algorithms be improved? (iii) In particular, can we improve the interval testing algorithm of Asashiba et al.?
